questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Kyoto because of the rich culture and deep history that the city embodies. Furthermore, I chose it with the hopes of getting to improve my Japanese language skills, because of the amount of Japanese to foreign people that live in the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I absolutely loved being on exchange at Ritsumeikan, and I would go back in a heartbeat. One thing that needs to change to make the academic part be less stressful is to decrease the amount of necessary credits for courses. The amount of lectures and exams were very stressful and I had almost no free time because of the 15 credit requirement. I had classes 18 hrs a week, which was simply too much. After speaking with the International center at Ritsumeikan, they would recommend 12 credits total as a maximum for attended classes, which I agree with.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was made easier because of the wonderful RM’s at my dorm and the flyers the international center gave out. The people at my dorm were very helpful in helping me find information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Again, the RM’s at my dorm and the people living there were so helpful, both helping me going to the ward office and helping me fill out all the necessary documents.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was great, because Ritsumeikan already had off campus dorm options that we could choose to stay at, and the process of arriving was simple and easy to figure out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You cannot live on campus at Ritsumeikan, but the dorm options are amazing and close to campus!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The process of registering for all of the different required things was difficult and I needed to get help doing all of them, also because every document was written in Japanese, which did not make it easier.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to register for many things. These included the national health care insurance, a pension service, a CO-OP service for getting books and meals at campus, and aside from that we needed to open a bank account at the post office, which was a difficult task to begin with.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The RM’s at my dorm were very helpful during every step of the way, and they certainly made the amount of bureaucracy and paperwork easier to handle.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was given a list of available classes aside from the Japanese language course, that I could register for. I got the ones that I chose there, no issue, but they did not match my wishes from back home exactly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rely on your RM’s and ask the international center for help when you need it! They are very helpful and want to aid you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was beyond satisfied with the Japanese language courses, the quality of classes there were amazing and I would recommend the IJL courses to anyone interested in learning Japanese academically. Otherwise, the level of quality was mixed. Some of the courses were very superficial, and rarely dug deep into the material we were studying, which I thought was a shame.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. We were generally speaking more students than in my Japan studies courses, and the Japanese language courses were only in Japanese and were way more conversation and listening focused than back at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in the IJL level 4 courses in listening and speaking, comprehension and writing, furthermore I was enrolled in the RCE (courses in english) courses Cross Cultural Encounters 1, Japanese Poetry, Japanese Culture and Field research and a Calligraphy class.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend all the courses apart from the Cross Cultural Encounters class, on the count of it unfortunately being a bit too superficial academically for my taste.

questions.answer: I was shocked by the amount of things we had to pay for in terms of required services, and we had to pay three different deposits, which was surprising to me.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Bear in mind that the personal expenses were based on my shopping and leisure

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a wide variety, everything from a cycling club to a theatre club and manga club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go bouldering in the gym Adsummum in the Shinkyogoku shopping street Teramachi, go karaokeing and hiking in the nearby forests and mountains.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the many museums, shrines, temples, restaurants, bars and go hang out near the Kamogawa river.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a bit daunting at first, but I eventually adjusted well and I miss it a lot. It was harder to adjust to coming home again.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people, go to social events at the Borders Beyond Plaza (BBP) and practice your Japanese language skills!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I have a tattoo, and I did meet some prejudice there, not being let in to fitness gyms and onsens regularly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: So many things. I got to experience the many festivals/matsuri in Kyoto, which was fantastic.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say that it is a good idea to get the Randen pass if you live in the Tokiwa dorm, join the BBP events and to not only focus on classes, but go explore Japan a bit while you are there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pick a maximum of 12 credits worth of classes, more WILL be stressful and leave you with minimal time for anything but classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have gotten some friends that I cherish a lot and experienced things that I will treasure for the rest of my life. Furthermore, I really improved my Japanese language skills, which I am very satisfied with.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was definitely living in the Japanese summer heat. The temperatures exceed 40 degrees sometimes, so prepare for heatwaves if you go during the summer.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
